Author: @usernamedkjahstill5003
Content: If you select "I won't do it" in Death Stranding 2: On the Beach, you trigger a "Groundhog Day"-style Easter egg where the game briefly replays the preceding events before returning you to the cutscene with Fragile, forcing the same dialogue choice. After refusing a second time, you hear Sam shout "No!" as the game shows a photograph of him on the mountain, and then you are returned to the cutscene once more, but this time you will no longer have the option to refuse, making the choice inconsequential to the overall story. This sequence serves as a playful nod from Kojima to player agency before the story inevitably moves forward.

Content:
@jacksepticeye, I watched your whole Death Stranding 1 playthrough and I totally get why you liked the game. It was a very interesting game that was focused on storytelling (and that's probably why a lot of people didn't like it as much as you!). The storytelling was pretty solid all in all, the game looked beautiful, the production quality of the video and audio was top-notch, the atmospheres (even experienced 2nd hand) were spectacular, and the story was very interesting even if certain aspects were unnecessarily convoluted or even a little hokey once it was all said and done. But I watched the whole playthrough recently because I had started watching it when you first released it and just never got past episode 2 or so and decided when DS2 came out and saw you were starting a lets-play of it, that I'd watch the rest. 

I could tell why you really got sucked in and enjoyed DS1 and I'm here to watch DS2 because first - I have long enjoyed watching your lets-plays due to your appreciation for both stories and storytelling. Most youtubers doing them seem far more interested in action and gameplay while I can appreciate those things, I'm WAY more engaged by good stories - something you find a lot more of to play through than any other youtuber I know of. Secondly, because I really enjoyed your playthrough of DS1 and am now eager to enjoy watching you play through DS2. =)

Author: @jaredclimer8882
Content: Sean I’m sure you’ve probably beaten the whole game by the time these videos come out but just a few tips that I noticed while watching this video that you seem to have missed. If you come to a river that’s too wide for one ladder and you have more then one ladder then you get a prompt when placing a ladder to combine them and make one extra long ladder. Also as far as dropping your entire backpack at the time fall shelter you don’t get a prompt for it you just have to hold triangle and your backpack gets offloaded where you’re standing so do that at a time fall shelter if you wanna go fight something and not worry about your cargo getting damaged. Lastly when you’re using guns or grenades you don’t have to go into your inventory menu every time you run out in order to switch to fresh ones. If you have another gun of the same type or you have more grenades of the same type then just aim with the empty one and press O and it automatically switches out the empty equipment with a new one from your backpack. Sorry I know the message is long winded but watching the video and seeing little things like this that are major quality of life improvements from the first game going unnoticed just makes my OCD scream.

Content: I watched a video earlier this year about Hideo Kojima's career that led him to "Death Stranding." Content:
How to make the perfect grilled cheese: 

Instructions:

Prepare Your Bread & Butter:

Lightly butter one side of each slice of bread, extending all the way to the edges. If using mayonnaise, spread a thin layer on the outside of the bread instead of butter. This creates an unbelievably crispy, golden crust.
Pro Tip: For an even crispier exterior, grate a tiny bit of Parmesan cheese directly onto the buttered side of the bread. This will create a delicious, savory crust.
Assemble the Cheese:

Place one slice of bread, buttered-side down, in your cold skillet.
Layer your cheese blend evenly over the bread. Don't overstuff it, or the cheese won't melt properly.
Top with the second slice of bread, buttered-side up.
The Low and Slow Cook (Crucial!):

Place the skillet over low to medium-low heat. This is the most important step for an amazing grilled cheese. High heat will burn the bread before the cheese melts.
Cook for 4-6 minutes per side, or until the bread is deeply golden brown and the cheese is fully melted and oozing.
Don't rush it! You want the heat to gently permeate the sandwich, melting the cheese slowly and evenly.
Press Gently (Optional): After a few minutes on the first side, you can gently press down on the sandwich with your spatula. This helps create more contact with the pan and encourages even browning and melting. Don't flatten it completely.
Check for Doneness:

Carefully lift a corner of the sandwich to check the browning. Once it's a beautiful golden brown, carefully flip it.
Continue cooking on the second side until equally golden and the cheese is completely molten.
Serve Immediately:

Transfer the grilled cheese to a plate.
For the best experience, slice it diagonally. The diagonal cut reveals the beautiful layers of melted cheese and makes it easier to eat.
